_readme: Projects that open in place from the home wall (a tile with data-project=<slug>). Source of truth for tools/build_projects.py, which builds media/projects/<slug>/ and writes one <template data-proj> per project into index.html. Monitor 1 is on program when the project opens; type loop = the wall's own loop (media/loops). Paths: PV/ = Desktop/Production Visuals, S/ = this repo.

projects.title: HALFCOURT
projects.line: A world tour played on half a court, so the whole identity is built from one half: the arc.
projects.idea: 3×3 basketball is played on half a court, under a twelve-second shot clock. HALFCOURT draws both with one line: the 6.75 m arc over the baseline, cut into twelve segments that fill as the clock runs and flash at the siren. Every graphic lives in the arc on twelve ticks: the score bug, the lower third, the replay wipe, the scoreboard, and the real arcs painted on six courts.
projects.role: Concept, identity, wordmark and typography, broadcast graphics, motion, compositing and tracking, original score, creative code, front-end
facts: The 2-point arc is the mark and the shot clock: twelve segments, one per second
One render(t) draws the film, the posters' type, the scoreboard and the live page
The volt arc sits on the real paint of six courts, laid by homography
The live page before its first frame
projects.note: HALFCOURT is a fictional 3×3 world tour. Self-initiated concept. Not affiliated with any league or federation. Teams, players, stops and dates are invented. Footage, photographs and mockups (phone, billboard, LED scoreboard, TV, jerseys): Freepik (licensed). Sound effects (dribble, swish, crowd): Pixabay. Typefaces: Panchang and Switzer by Indian Type Foundry (Fontshare, ITF Free Font License). Music: original, composed in code on a twelve-step grid with the real dribble as the kick.

projects.title: JURASSIC PARK
projects.line: One fan poster, one double exposure: the T-rex keeps its face, and the island it rules lives inside its neck.
projects.idea: A double exposure is two negatives on one sheet. The first is the predator; the second is the misty island it owns. A mask painted along the jaw keeps the teeth and the eye, and lets the jungle into the skull and neck. Below it the same photograph spills onto the paper and becomes the ground, so the neck has no edge. The live page hands you the dial.
projects.role: Concept, art direction, double exposure and retouching, colour, title design, creative code, motion, front-end
facts: A Midjourney T-rex and one photograph of a misty jungle. Nothing else is in the picture
Painted along the jaw: the teeth and the eye stay, the skull and neck become the island
Inside the neck the jungle is screened in, outside it is printed on the paper, so they meet without a seam

projects.title: BIGGER.
projects.line: Every designer has met this client. Few have watched him eat the logo.
projects.idea: “Make the logo bigger” is the most famous client note in the world. BIGGER. finally explains it: the client is a pigeon in a tailored suit, and the perfect minimal logo is a seed. Every click grows it, the music climbs a semitone, the designer sweats, and then a stomach growls. The seed is also the full stop of the wordmark, so the pigeon eats that too.
projects.role: Concept, script, character design, rig and animation, creative code, typography, sound design and original score, front-end

projects.title: ACCORD
projects.line: An eau de parfum built like a chord: three notes are three tones, and the light on the glass tunes them as the bottle turns.
projects.idea: In perfumery an accord is a few notes that blend into one scent; in music, a few tones that sound as one. ACCORD does both literally: bergamot, iris and amber are three tones tuned 4 : 5 : 6, and the mark is their sum. One 3D scene lights the bottle, the box and the bag; each note has its own lamp, so the glass itself plays the chord.
projects.role: Concept, identity, typography, 3D and lighting, compositing, original score, creative code, front-end

projects.title: INTERSTELLAR
projects.line: A fan poster series where gravity bends everything, the poster too: the title sits behind a ray-traced black hole and comes out curved.
projects.idea: Two unofficial posters share one grid, one wide typeface and one rule: the world bends the title. In GARGANTUA a Schwarzschild ray tracer bends a real Milky Way, a disk of real fire and the title itself, down to its upside-down ghost on the photon ring. In MILLER the horizon crosses the astronaut's helmet and the water round his legs is computed, reflection and all.

projects.title: UMBRA
projects.line: An identity that exists for one minute: 139 pillars on a Belgrade plaza whose shadows spell the name only at 18:47 on 21 June.
projects.idea: UMBRA is a fictional architecture biennale whose name is never drawn. Cut into fifteen rows of concrete pillars, each exactly as tall as its shadow must be long when the sun stands at 288° and 15° over Belgrade, the field says nothing all day, gathers for half an hour and reads for one minute. One WebGL engine computes the real sun and rendered everything here.

projects.title: STRUJA
projects.line: A festival identity that is a behaviour, not a file: one line of light on the river, drawn by the music, cutting through the name.
projects.idea: One line of sodium streetlight on the Sava. At rest it is the river’s real course through Belgrade; the music bends it, every kick sends a wave downstream, and at the drop the line unwinds. One custom WebGL engine draws it from the track, and the same engine rendered the film, the posters and every screen.
projects.role: Concept, identity, motion, original score, creative code, front-end
facts: The line’s rest shape, from map data
projects.note: STRUJA is a fictional festival and a self-initiated project. Water footage and mockups: Freepik (licensed). Stage plates: Midjourney. River data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL). Typeface: Science Gothic (SIL OFL).
